newsitem.title: UK: EU Commissioner Kinnock expects EU stability deal.
newsitem.headline: EU Commissioner Kinnock expects EU stability deal.

text.p: European Union Commissioner Neil Kinnock said on Sunday he expects Germany and France to reach a deal on the pact underpinning Europe's planned single currency at the Amsterdam summit of EU leaders on Monday and Tuesday.

"I am led to believe from what I read that there will be a formulation that will enable Lionel Jospin to be assured that the enforcement of the stability pact will not be so severe...(and that it) will not be so loose as to alarm Helmut Kohl about the softness of the common currency," he said.
Kinnock, one of Britain's two members of the EU Commission, said he believed media reports of the row between Germany and France had been too pessimistic about the chances of a deal.

"At the time when the leaders debate them there's likely to be more refinement and readiness to accept sustainable consensus than might be thought in the various kinds of report... that we see in the weeks before any summit," Kinnock, the EU Transport Commissioner, told the British Broadcasting Corp.
Jospin, France's new socialist Prime Minister, said on Saturday after two hours of talks with French President Jacques Chirac he was "not pessimistic" about the outcome of the summit.
Jospin, swept to power in an upset parliamentary election victory on May 1, raised objections to the stability pact for the first time a week ago.
Jospin has said the new government remains committed to monetary union but wants a fundamentally different approach putting job creation on a par with monetary stability.

The French government's demands, at odds with Germany's view of the single currency, have thrown preparations for the single currency into disarray and overshadowed the Amsterdam summit, called to finalise a treaty to reform the European Union's treaties.
